verdicts.reason: Both are near-identical. In each, the orange 'Start Free Week' CTA is jammed against the end of 'alive' with almost no gap and sits on the cropped yellow circle, the badges are tiny, and the logo floats centred and away from the left-aligned headline column. B's phone has a little more top and bottom margin than A's, whose phone nearly touches both canvas edges.

A puts the CTA flush against the left canvas edge and butted into the 'K' of 'Keep', so the action reads before the headline. Its phone also nearly touches the bottom edge. B keeps headline then CTA in reading order, but the CTA still crowds 'alive' and overlaps the cropped circle, and its badges are tiny.

A has the CTA on the left, jammed against the left edge and touching 'Keep', which breaks reading order. B has the same CTA collision and also wraps the headline to leave 'alive' on its own line. B's subcopy also shrinks to near-illegible fine print set inline with the badges, which flattens the hierarchy.

A breaks the design apart. The logo is reduced to a tiny mark at the bottom beside illegible subcopy, the 'NO GEAR' badge floats alone above the headline away from 'AUDIO COACHING', 'alive' is orphaned, and the phone runs into the top and bottom edges. B is coherent but has its CTA jammed against the left edge and touching 'Keep', in the wrong reading order.
